title: feat(security): the record field-access answer says whether the record itself is writable
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBHS5r3FWzbMqPq7Ve6wZPUp)_

Fixes #27175

Ruling-ref: 6457467702
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — `skills/**` names no reader of the record field-access answer (`git grep -n "field-access\|getRecordFieldAccess\|fieldAccess" -- skills/` is empty); the hand-written page that does, `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`, is updated here

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:记录的字段访问答案(`GET /data/{object}/{id}/field-access`)新增 `writable: boolean`,表示「这条记录本身能不能被更新」。
- 怎么算的:不是另写一套判断。plugin-security 保留它注册到引擎上的那个授权中间件函数,对这条记录跑一次「按 id 更新、空 payload」的模拟操作,在链尾、引擎执行器(钩子、校验、写库、审计)之前截停;链尾再问 plugin-sharing 的按 id 写闸(抽成 `SharingService.admitsByIdWrite`,其中间件也只调用它)。任何一处拒绝即 `false`。
- 风险与回滚:探测不写任何东西:上下文用副本,不推进权限缓存 epoch(单测钉住),dogfood 钉住无审计行、记录不变。`editable` 不变。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/record-row-write-probe.ts`,`security-plugin.ts` 的 `isRecordRowWritable`,`plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` 的 `admitsByIdWrite`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/record-field-access-when.dogfood.test.ts`,预期 10/10(他人拥有的 `public_read` 行 `writable: false` 且 PATCH 403;可写行 `true` 且 PATCH 200)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地;随后 ui 席位接 #27138。

## What changes

**One row-level verdict on the record projection.** `GetRecordFieldAccessResponseSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) gains `writable: boolean`: whether the caller may update this record at all, judged by the write gate on the stored row. `false` means an update is refused whole, whatever it changes. The describe names in customer language what `true` does not cover. `editable` is unchanged and stays field-level; its describe now points at `writable`. `ISecurityService.getRecordFieldAccess` (`contracts/security-service.ts`) documents the member. The shape is a boolean only: the gate has no closed row-reason vocabulary (its refusals are `PERMISSION_DENIED` with a catalog sentence, or sharing's `FORBIDDEN`), and a boolean discloses nothing more than the PATCH would.

**The verdict is the gate's own code, run in a would-pass mode.** A by-id update is refused for its row by two engine middlewares, so the verdict asks both, through their own code:

- *plugin-security's authorization middleware.* `registerAuthzMiddleware` now returns the handler it registers, and `SecurityPlugin` keeps it (`authzMiddleware`). `isRecordRowWritable` hands that same function a synthetic by-id `update` of the row (empty payload, a copy of the caller's context, the opCtx shape `engine.update()` builds) and a terminal `next()` that ends the probe with a sentinel only `probeRecordRowWrite` catches (`record-row-write-probe.ts`). So every step a real update meets runs: the engine-owned write guard, the delegated-admin gate, principal and posture resolution, the `requiredPermissions` AND-gate (1.5), the CRUD grant (2), the access-depth stamp (2.6), the RLS pre-image with the ownership floor and its sharing deferral (2.7), the controlled-by-parent master (2.8), and the payload gates over an empty payload (2.5, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7). Any throw is `false`. The handler body is unchanged except for one guard (below).
- *plugin-sharing's middleware.* Its by-id gate (`canEdit` / `canDelete`, the delegator's gate, then the `probeAuthoredRowWrite` deferral) moved into one method, `SharingService.admitsByIdWrite(object, id, verb, context)`. The middleware now calls it and refuses exactly when it answers `false`; the refusal messages and log lines are unchanged. The probe's terminal asks the same method with the context as the security middleware stamped it (`__writeScope`, an external principal's grant), which is what the sharing middleware reads in the real chain (it registers at `kernel:ready`, after the security middleware, so it runs inside it). `byIdWriteGateInstalled` is set when the middleware is installed; under `enforce: false` no by-id write meets the gate, and the probe skips it too.

A transferred record shows why both legs are needed: its former creator passes the security middleware's ownership floor (`created_by == current_user.id`) and is refused only by sharing.

**No side effects.** The engine's executor, where `beforeUpdate` hooks, validation, the driver write, `afterUpdate` hooks and audit run, sits after the last middleware, so the probe never reaches it. Before that point the handler refuses, reads, and stamps the operation and the context; the probe owns the operation and passes a copy of the context. Read through the closure for anything else that writes: no emits, no audit, no counters. The one write to shared state is the permission-set memo epoch the handler advances on a write when the engine does not own that seam; it is now skipped for a probe (`isRowWriteProbe`, a module-private symbol on the operation context that no request can carry). Caches that any read fills (permission-set resolution) fill as they would on a read.

**Not in the verdict (declared residuals, named in the describe):**
- a pending approval's record lock: a `beforeUpdate` hook in plugin-approvals, judged on the values sent (the status mirror field stays writable), with its own reader, `IApprovalService.getRecordLock`, which the record detail page already reads;
- conditional read-only rules and validation rules on the values a save sends;
- an external datasource that refuses writes (engine `assertWriteAllowed`, object-level);
- other plugins' middlewares for their own objects (mail, attachments).
So `true` never means "this save will succeed"; `false` always means the gate refuses the whole row.

**Known effect:** a probe that is refused logs the gate's usual refusal `warn` line (for example "Access denied: not permitted to update this 'rfa_notice' record (row-level security)"), as a refused PATCH does. Suppressing it would mean probe-awareness at every refusal site; left as is.

Files:
- `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`; regenerated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/record-row-write-probe.ts` (new), `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` (returns the handler; the probe epoch guard; header note), `security-plugin.ts` (`authzMiddleware`, `isRecordRowWritable`, `writable` in `getRecordFieldAccess`).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` (`admitsByIdWrite`, `byIdWriteGateInstalled`), `sharing-plugin.ts` (the middleware calls it; the flag is set where the middleware is installed).
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-field-access-when.dogfood.test.ts`, `fixtures/record-field-access-fixture.ts`.
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`: the projection bullet now describes `writable`.
- Changesets (root `.changeset/`): `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, each `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. The spec changeset carries a "Supersedes, in the same release" paragraph for the unreleased #26594 note that lists the answer's old shape.

`@objectstack/client` (`data.fieldAccess`) and `@objectstack/rest` relay the answer unchanged and pick the member up from the spec type; their src does not move.

## Why

#27175 / #27138: a user who may read a shared record but not change it opens Edit, fills the form, saves, and loses the work to a refusal of the whole update. The permission contract promises a client never advertises an edit the gate refuses. Ruling 6457467702 (letter B) forbids a client-side re-derivation, so the server has to say it, and triage 6465932161 asks for the gate's own computation returned as one boolean. With `writable`, ui seat 2 can dispatch #27138: `RecordFieldAccessScope` reads it and the edit surfaces show the record read-only when it is false.

## Verification

Head `58e92a401` (four commits plus a merge of `origin/main` `fd73f2b39`, which touched none of these files). Run on the shared container under `os-verify-lock`.

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 108 derived commands, each run and its exit recorded. `--ran` reconciliation: 108 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. 106 exited 0 on the first run. `spec check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (their prerequisite, built dist of client-react, studio and the knowledge/embedder packages, was absent); after building those packages both exited 0. Nothing in the diff changed between the runs.
- Build: `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/dogfood^...' --filter=@objectstack/plugin-sharing --filter=@objectstack/plugin-security` exit 0, again after the main merge. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` exit 0 (it found `content/docs/references/**` stale once; `--fix` regenerated only that, committed).
- Tests: plugin-security 236 files, 5104 passed / 45 skipped; plugin-sharing 57 files, 1280 passed; rest `record-field-access-route.test.ts` 5/5; `typecheck` of spec, plugin-security and plugin-sharing exit 0.
- Dogfood: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/record-field-access-when.dogfood.test.ts` 10/10. New legs: the `public_read` row another user owns answers `writable: false` and both PATCHes answer 403; the draft and approved contracts and the member's own notice answer `true` and their PATCH answers 200; three probes leave the stored row equal and add no `sys_audit_log` update row, while one real save adds exactly one (the `AuditPlugin` is booted for this).
- Unit pins (`security-plugin.test.ts`, `[#27175] writable`): `writable` equals a by-id update through the same handler, inside and outside the RLS write scope, and with an object grant lacking edit; the epoch is not advanced and the caller's context is not stamped (a real update through the same handler does advance it); the sharing leg is asked with `__writeScope` stamped and decides the verdict both ways, and is skipped when `byIdWriteGateInstalled` is false; no registered middleware answers `false`. `sharing-service.test.ts`: the middleware refuses exactly where `admitsByIdWrite` answers false, for update and delete, four (row, user) pairs each, and asks the method once per write.
- Ablations (each from a committed state, restored with `git restore`, rebuilt): `probeRecordRowWrite` forced to `true` reds 3 unit pins and the dogfood `public_read` leg; the epoch guard removed reds the no-side-effect pin alone.

## Out-of-scope findings (for seat 1 to file)

- The approvals record lock is not in `writable` (see residuals). The record detail page reads `getRecordLock`; whether the edit dialog (`ModalForm` / `DrawerForm` / the edit page) does is the ui half's question when #27138 is dispatched: an approval-locked record is the same "edit, then lose the work" case.
- The client (`packages/client/src/index.ts` `data.fieldAccess`) and rest route comments describe the answer as the field projection only; accurate, but they do not name `writable`. Left untouched to keep those packages out of the release.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [ ] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. (No formatter ran. `pnpm lint` is CI's run.)
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request. (The branch is the harness-pinned `claude/project-thread-askd75`, named in the claim.)
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English. (The 维护者速读 block is in Chinese by the repo's dispatch rule.)
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
